reviews.review:
Ah man, what a power fantasy. The combat is a bit simplistic yet feels super meaty and satisfying. In this game you do not have to choose between the melee or ranged path, you are a certified badass and lethal at any distance. The game 100% consists of you killing everything to death and it is glorious as you make enemies around you disappear into puffs of red mist. 

Puzzles? Nah bro. Overindulgent, tedious cut scenes? Nope. Messing with skill trees, experience points or gear upgrades? GTFO with that fluff. Looting dead enemies, surely? Not here.
Perhaps the single strongest element in this game is the pacing. There is no filler. It's all go, all the time, and you always feel like you're doing something important and advancing the plot. 
Peppered throughout the campaign are these pods that do give you access to new weapons but honestly the combat is so damn fun I never felt the need for more toys, just more enemies to purge.

Surprisingly there is also a pretty good narrative going on here, I enjoyed the story more than I usually do in these types of games. I'm peripherally aware of the 40k universe but know next to nothing about it. This game I think is a solid introduction, I never felt like I was missing anything important. 
The art direction is absolutely amazing and it elevates the dated graphics considerably. 

The elephant in the room is the price. I'm pretty sure I picked up this game in a bundle or something, and I'm not sure if its a regional mishap or whatever, but steam lists the game at $75 australian, which is a little steep for a sub 10 hour campaign in a 10+ year old game.
Story line is great, graphics for the time were really good. Offered PVP game play
I wrote a poorly worded, disheartening review of this game. Like a weak, weak human, once I got past the trouble I was having, I fell back in love with it. I beat the game recently, it was kick ass.

A very fun corridor shooter with violent melee combat from the 360 / PS3 generation.
Story wise, it does expect you to have a ground knowledge of the 40K universe to really follow what's happening.

If Kratos had a penchant for absolutely enormous firearms of all varieties and no patience for puzzles (or anything other than wholesale, righteous destruction of his foes), he would have fit right into this game. An oldie now but still very much a goodie.
